Package com.bilt.pos.session

Class ReversalFlow<T>

java.lang.Object
com.bilt.pos.session.ReversalFlow<T>
Type Parameters:
T - the reversal's result type
public final class ReversalFlow<T> extends Object
The reversal chain returned by the voidTransaction() and refund operations of CheckoutSession (this session's own payment) and ReversalSession (a referenced prior sale).

Registering handlers sends nothing; the reversal steps run blocking on the calling thread when execute(), get(), or getOrNull() is invoked. When a step fails, the onError handler decides how to proceed — ReversalDecision.RETRY, ReversalDecision.SKIP, or ReversalDecision.ABORT. Without a handler the default policy applies: a failed money step (the card or stored value leg) aborts; a failed loyalty movement riding along with a money step is skipped (the terminal can retry it via store-and-forward); a failed loyalty movement that is the substance of the reversal aborts.


 session.voidTransaction()
     .onError((step, error) -> step == ReversalStep.AWARD
             ? ReversalDecision.SKIP : ReversalDecision.ABORT)
     .onSuccess(result -> register.printVoidReceipt(result))
     .execute();

    • onSuccess

    • onError

      public ReversalFlow<T> onError(BiFunction<ReversalStep,SessionError,ReversalDecision> handler)
      Called when a step fails; the returned ReversalDecision controls whether the flow retries the step, skips it, or aborts. A null decision counts as ReversalDecision.ABORT.

      A terminal failure the handler did not resolve with an abort — one before any step ran (a state rejection, a missing reference), or a reversal whose every step was skipped and therefore reversed nothing — is delivered with a null step; the returned decision is then ignored, there is nothing left to resolve.

      Because of that null-step delivery, a handler that switches on the step must guard for null first — an exception thrown from the handler would mask the very failure being delivered. Null-safe comparisons, as in the class example (step == ReversalStep.AWARD ? SKIP : ABORT), need no guard.
